scope: Readonly architecture proposal; not integrated code or runtime proof
accepted: Durable resource allocations before creating artifact bytes
Cancellation intent before abort, drain, close, authenticated deletion, fsync and reservation release
Internal cleanup visibility separate from current-workspace public operations
Retain staged or uncertain restore evidence and original operation ownership
Filesystem free-space check is admission only, not an OS reservation
corrections: Prepared sqliteBytes=3GiB caps the main database only, not main plus rollback; its budget must add journal overhead
Upload preview/stage retains both decoded and transformed catalogs unless code safely removes one; charge both at peak
Preserve the existing cold restore prepared path and catalog/prepared known-file admission; proposed new layout and OWNER sibling assumptions do not fit current readers
Do not pass a freely trusted previousWorkspaceId into transfer storage or rebind only its owner header; prefer per-workspace transport journals with internal terminal cleanup
Do not refuse all legacy v1 imports once a v2 journal exists; implement conversion or exact bound completion while preserving valid legacy inputs
Do not delete unknown-operation orphan files based only on a marker/PID; preserve unattributed artifacts and charge or block admission
Match the existing POST/PUT client route and body contract; no proposed PATCH routes
Physical statfs accounting must be serialized against coordinator writers/cleanup, with conservative scratch attribution; proposal subtracts scanned bytes too broadly
next: Implement minimal artifact allocation and cleanup protocol after physical component bounds. Public coordinator and v1 coexistence remain open.
